factsheet.heading: Landscape Design
paragraphs: As the tour moves through the King’s Cross area, participants will explore the role of green spaces in shaping everyday urban life. Guided by a Landscape Architect, the walk examines how original design intentions are maintained, adapted, or reinterpreted over time by the people who inhabit and use these spaces. Through conversations with designers, planners, and local residents, the tour uncovers stories that reveal how public spaces are envisioned, experienced, and collectively shared.

Using storytelling as a lens, the tour traces King’s Cross as a landscape shaped by water, industry, reinvention, and visions of the future city. As one of London’s most prominent examples of large-scale urban regeneration and gentrification, King’s Cross provides a compelling setting for exploring how cities evolve, how identities are reshaped, and what these transformations might tell us about the urban future.
The walking tour will last approximately 2 to 2.5 hours. Participants are advised to wear comfortable, weather-appropriate footwear suitable for extended walking and standing.

factsheet.heading: Golden Key Academy
paragraphs: The Golden Key Academy is a course training up insightful and engaging guides dedicated to explaining London and bringing its many stories to life. This tour is part of a wider collection of tours created by Golden Key Academy guides for the Open House Festival celebrating their conclusion of the eight month course.
Further information on the Golden Key Academy can be found here https://open-city.org.uk/golden-key-academy
If you would like to attend this tour, please ensure you have booked a ticket before turning up.
